== Biography ==
{{Appalachia Sticker|lived|state=Pennsylvania|project=yes}}
'''Samuel Glasgow''' was born about 21 Jun 1786 in Antis, Blair, Pennsylvania.

Samuel died on 22 Jul 1829 in Huntingdon, Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania, United States, aged about 43. He was buried in Riverview Cemetery, Huntingdon, Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania.<ref name="Death_1">''Find a Grave'', database and images (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/206274001/samuel-glasgow: accessed), memorial page for Samuel Glasgow (unknown–22 Jul 1829), Find a Grave Memorial ID 206274001, citing Riverview Cemetery, Huntingdon, Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania, USA; Maintained by Mike Fleck (contributor 49238974). <br>{{FindAGrave|206274001}}</ref>

== Research Notes ==
According to a public tree, Samuel's parents were [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1549 John Glasgow (1758-1825)] and [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hunter-18237 Margaret Hunter (1759-1925)].

=== Probable family identification ===
[[Glasgow-3682|Mary Wilson Glasgow]], wife of Thomas Enyeart, is explicitly called daughter of Samuel and Mary (Wilson) Glasgow in the 1914 Fouse genealogy; her exact 1814/1875 dates and daughter Matilda agree.<ref name="Fouse1914">''Genealogy of the descendants of Theobald Fouse (Fauss)'' (1914), p. 74; [https://archive.org/details/genealogyofdesce01brum/page/n140/mode/1up original scan, IA leaf 140].</ref> [[Glasgow-2637|Benjamin Franklin Glasgow]] has the same named parental couple in his memorial-derived biography. Samuel of Huntingdon is the preferred existing father candidate for Mary (77% probable) and Benjamin (71% probable). The children name the same parental couple, Samuel Glasgow and Mary Wilson, in the Huntingdon, Pennsylvania family setting. Samuel Glasgow-1984 is the existing compatible Huntingdon man, with a contributed birth about 1786 in Antis and a held memorial death of 22 July 1829. These dates permit fatherhood in 1814 and 1827, at about 28 and 41. The shared full parental couple and locality give a stronger match than the forename Samuel alone. No inspected probate, household, church or cemetery record yet identifies Samuel Glasgow-1984 as this Mary Wilson’s husband or either child’s father. His approximate birth and locality are inherited profile claims, not newly verified records. The memorial pages were not freshly inspected. The memorial and 1914 book may share a source and are not independent proofs. A missing middle initial on Samuel’s profile is not a conflict; Benjamin’s captured account calls the father Samuel L. The identity remains open to another compatible Samuel. The exact percentage is a subjective assessment of the complete identification with the existing Samuel Glasgow-1984, not merely of a named Samuel father. The existing-profile identification remains probable. Mary Wilson is assessed separately as the reported mother; no numbered mother, spouse or upstream parent is assigned. The public-tree suggestion for Samuel’s own parents already present remains an unverified lead and is not adopted by these child assessments.
